notes: Web Package 899 / sos-cache-v899. Realtime performance: P2P transfer flow control, voice P2P E2EE, call relay health failover and ring latency. Secure incoming-call receiver starts on identity readiness (no outgoing-call priming). Security closure: mesh relay signals are recipient-bound P2pSecureV2 ciphertext only; outgoing call signaling is kind 1059 only (no 25050 downgrade on policy failure). First-group network-backed administration (israel-network). Group control panel behind a 6-digit admin PIN lock with server-side Admin 2FA (server PIN verifier + attestation signer; enforcement ships OFF until owner enrollment). User-centric group control UX (search, per-user role and permissions; saving disabled until the control plane is activated). Admin 2FA enforcement ON with the pinned production signer; root-only Gate 1.5 activation (attested genesis, no grants). Gate 2: owner-activated admission service delegation (single FINALIZE_MEMBERSHIP_ADMISSION capability, Admin 2FA attested). Gate 4: accessControlV2Scope (FULL | CONTROL_PLANE); CONTROL_PLANE keeps member content, P2P and the single-network UI as V2 off. ACCESS_CONTROL_V2 ships OFF. 899h: top-bar invite reconciles authority before the capability check (INVITE_USERS propagation); Worker-identity recovery via sealed F5B6-W handoff to the isolated signer and F5B5 reveal; truthful onboarding (no fake key field/buttons); logout/switch guarded until the recovery backup is confirmed. 899i: account creation includes the personal key — after Passkey the isolated signer saves SOS-personal-key-<fingerprint>.txt locally and returns only a non-secret completion (PERSONAL_KEY_EXPORTED); login accepts the key file. 899j: profile metadata is actually published (awaited typed signature, relay acks, monotonic created_at), avatar/cover stored as durable Blossom https URLs, profile page loads the signer; one newest-wins profile resolution for feed, conversations, public profile and group management (stub names are refreshed); the floating home group-management button is removed (menu entry only). 899k: per-user permission panel shows three primary permissions (הזמנת חברים, מחיקת פוסטים ותגובות, ניהול חברים) with short explanations; the other canonical capabilities are in a collapsed advanced section (UI only, protocol unchanged). 899l: MANAGE_MEMBERS description matches its effect (remove members and manage their membership state, no permission changes); pending joins are read-only with an automatic-approval status (no dead manual approve button; admission stays with the Admission Service). 899m: Phase 1 moderation and member control - four primary permissions (INVITE_USERS, MODERATE_CONTENT, MANAGE_MEMBERS, MANAGE_BLOCKLIST); per-user remove / block / unblock / user content (canonical blocklist + membership, Admin 2FA); blocked authors' posts, comments and videos are hidden in SOS by pubkey suppression from the verified blocklist (no relay deletion claimed); blocked members cannot post, comment, react, invite, use group control or P2P; report button on posts, videos and comments with private sealed per-moderator reports (kind 39010 wrap, no public report), moderator reports tab with statuses and badge; audit rows for content removal, block/unblock and report resolution. Multi-community network deferred. MD4 not started. Android/APK frozen. 899n: existing users are added directly from group control through the canonical GRANT_ACTIVE membership transition (ROOT or MANAGE_MEMBERS, Admin 2FA, relay readback; no invite, no capabilities granted); invites are for new users only - 24h maximum lifetime, single use, active list plus collapsed history with ACTIVE / USED / EXPIRED / REVOKED statuses; no join-approval UI. 899o: israel-network default membership — SOS-registered accounts (own email-registry 37377) are members unless REMOVED/BLOCKED; owner-authorized reviewed reconciliation via canonical GRANT_ACTIVE (no capabilities); no add-to-group button for normal users in the default community; Admin 2FA control attestations pushed to the admission service. 899p: group control "כל המשתמשים" directory - every known SOS identity (members, legacy SOS accounts with their own registry record or SOS profile, removed, blocked) with avatar, name, short id, status and last activity; filters and search; per-user drawer. A reviewed legacy account can be confirmed as a plain member, or saving "ניהול הרשאות" completes canonical membership first and then applies exactly the chosen permissions (Admin 2FA; removed / blocked never re-added; arbitrary Nostr keys rejected; no automatic capability or invite authority). Temporary membership-gap panel removed from the UI. 899q: moderator deletion of other users' posts and comments uses the same canonical path as ROOT (signed target, Admin 2FA attestation, relay ack and readback before success; failure restores the item and shows an error); the video feed subscribes to group moderation (39002) and its attestations (39004) so removals reach every client live and after refresh; invite menu shown only with INVITE_USERS or ROOT and updated live; group control menu only for ROOT or management capabilities (moderators get a reports-only entry, direct open denied); user directory avatars use the shared newest-profile resolver with an initials fallback. Durable moderation: a finalized removal is replayed on its Admin 2FA attestation (issued only after the creation-time authority check), so revoking a moderator stops new removals without undoing old ones; historical moderation is fetched per visible target (#d, then the bound attestations by #e), not from the newest N events. 899r: the video feed renders without waiting for likes/comments/shares; engagement hydrates in the background with bounded relay queries, so a slow or dead relay can no longer leave the fresh guest or signed-in feed black. 899s: the Videos feed shows local native video and images only (a YouTube link alone never qualifies; YouTube stays on other surfaces); suppressed authors cannot re-enter through the display fallback; up to 3 native cards warm in parallel and mount in feed order; boot releases when 2 of the top 6 posts are ready; feed order is canonical (createdAt / boost) and never changed by cache state; public media streams from a canonical, de-duplicated candidate list (local cache first, then declared hash mirrors, preferred Blossom, other mirrors, original, and files.sovbit.host last) with fast 404 fallback; background caching only for the centered, playing video (queue max 3, 160MB per session, skipped under Save-Data, SHA-256 verified); new posts after EOSE and periodic refresh auto-mount without Home while keeping the centered card. 899s.9: Linked Devices product UX — mobile camera scan / desktop SOSPAIR1 QR; remove legacy MD2 debug modal and synthetic QR fallback; single event owner; Web MD3/T2 issuance remains OFF; no W3/MD5. Source: scoped from Stage5 UX2 onto baseline 899s.8 (d1bcc51). 899s.10: UX3 Guest Desktop QR-first welcome + continue-as-guest; Desktop menu reopen; Mobile Linked Devices page; chat-request-logger Filter-shape telemetry fix (no flatMap throw on MD2 subscribeMany); Web MD3/T2 still OFF. 899s.11: UX4 Guest QR welcome simplified to single Continue-as-Guest action with auto-refresh of expired pairing QR; truthful Mobile Web T2-unavailable messaging (no fake APK mandate); nsec Uint8Array decode fallback for native WebView login. Web MD3/T2 issuance remains OFF. Android existing-key import clear-before-write is QA APK only. 899s.12: Linked Devices settings menu icon (fa-desktop) — fa-laptop-mobile was missing from the FA kit used by SOS. 899s.13: Desktop SOSPAIR1 QR render sharper/larger (HiDPI canvas, quiet zone 4); native APK Linked Devices menu opens CameraX PhoneIssuer when SosNativeShell is present; Web T2 issuance remains OFF. 899s.14: Desktop MD2 PoP Schnorr via dynamic @noble/curves (nostr-tools CDN lacks schnorr) — fixes HANDSHAKING stall after optical SOSPAIR1; relay primary nos.lol. 899s.15: Production Web T2 PhoneIssuer + MD2 openMd2Transport + emergency-wrapper publish contract + Worker AUTHORIZE_LINKED_DEVICE (owner PRODUCTION FIRST). 899s.16: Linked Devices shows a persistent Hebrew status when Trusted Signer is not ready (VAULT_NOT_READY) or Passkey enrollment is missing; sanitized MD2/T2 phase logs; Signer reports each approval error once with vault state. MD2 alone never marks LINKED. 899s.17: Desktop linking opens a session-bound account approval instead of a bare signer import page. A signed-in account can complete that once through the existing sealed handoff; a legacy key file uses the same session-bound import. Neither path marks the desktop linked. 899s.18: one QR scan continues in the same tab to the signer ceremony (no popup after MD2). Passkey enrollment, when missing, is the same device approval. The phone says the computer is connected only after a verified desktop link. 899s.19: the ceremony opens /authorize-linked-device directly so the pairing request is not dropped by the .html redirect. 899s.22: a same-tab approval waits for the issuance flag before it is accepted or discarded. 899s.23: the desktop verifies the root signature and stores the device before it acknowledges the phone. 899s.24: a QR scan authorizes one desktop link from the local signing vault without passkey, screen lock, or leaving SOS. 899s.25: after that verified link the guest QR sheet closes and the same public account opens on the desktop. The root key stays on the phone. Message history is not copied. 899s.26: a verified linked desktop is an account session. Profile, conversations, delegated chat and call signaling use the device key and the root-signed authorization. History, when the phone already has it, is re-wrapped to the device. The root key is not copied. 899s.27: linked history travels as an encrypted kind-1050 bundle on the same relays that already accept private chat. 899s.30: a verified linked desktop stops guest P2P, decrypts device-addressed envelopes with its device key, and a DataChannel delivery no longer skips encrypted relay copies for other authorized devices. History is not reported complete when attachments or oversized text are omitted. 899s.31: a desktop send waits for a real relay OK, replaces the optimistic bubble, and syncs that outgoing message to the phone. Incoming chat is filed on the account conversation. Call rings are copied to linked devices. A linked device heartbeat is an authorized device principal. 899s.32: a linked-device chat signature is checked on a plain event copy, so a valid D_sign event is not rejected after the integrity snapshot is frozen. Device-delivery copies stay on the account conversation. One logical message id covers the DataChannel and the relay. A call answer from an authorized device is applied to that account, and the first answer cancels the other devices. 899s.33: a device key that presents a valid root-signed MD3 authorization is filed on that account, and a later contact create for the same device key cannot open a second conversation. 899s.39: a linked desktop keeps its own send in the other account's conversation, and ordinary text is copied to that account's authorized devices even when the recipient phone is offline. 899s.40: the phone pulls account-addressed chat, so a desktop send still appears on the phone when the live subscription misses it. 899s.41: a verified sibling copy is kept when the relay snapshot is frozen, so the phone files the desktop's outgoing message. 899s.42: a phone file sent over the data channel is also copied to the sender's other devices, and a self-chat file is not marked delivered when no authorized device received it. 899s.43: self-chat files use a direct data channel to the other authorized device and stay pending when that device is offline; history is sent in pages instead of dropping older messages. 899s.44: a desktop file that finishes on the data channel is also copied to the sender's phone. 899s.45: a linked desktop accepts a same-account data-channel signal on its device key and answers with that key, without the root key. 899s.46: the same desktop decrypts the file offer with that device key. 899s.47: a linked desktop seals a self-chat file offer with its device key and sends it on the open data channel. 899s.50: after a verified link the desktop requests history by itself, and the phone sends the account conversations in encrypted pages that fit the chat envelope, including tombstones and available attachment bytes. 899s.51: history acknowledgements are checkpointed, large historical files prefer the data channel, and sync progress sits beside the SO-CALL logo. 899s.53: one history snapshot is reused per device while the conversations are unchanged, file transfer waits for a real data channel instead of probing every file, and relay subscriptions plus diagnostic logs are bounded.
